items.heading: Chemistry Has an Unusual Split
items.text: Chemistry has an unusual split. Many of its best-known employers write a master's into the rule.

items.heading: The Order Is a Judgement
items.text: The order is a judgement about how far income and independence can stretch with skill and proof, not about prestige. Chemistry with data or teaching content leads because the skill sells to many customers. QC, testing labs, formulation, tutoring and plant roles come next because each has a business layer.

items.heading: A Pay Line Means Little
items.text: A pay line means little without the filters in front of it. This ledger uses official notices and named sources, and it leaves out the unsourced ranges most career blogs print.

rows: Apply through JAM 2027 (IIT Kharagpur). Applications close on 19 October 2026, the exam is on 14 February 2027 and results come on 18 March 2027. About 3,000 seats across participating IITs. Each admitting institute sets its own subject rule, so read the eligibility page for your target programme.
A final-year or finished BSc can apply. Qualifying is not admission.

The official eligibility table lets students of a three-year BSc sit step in the third year or after finishing, to seek master's admission at IITs and IISc. There is a Chemistry (CY) paper, and the Life Sciences (XL) paper carries a 25-mark Chemistry section.
You can appear. It does not open jobs that name an MSc, such as BARC or DRDO.
A master's at 55 percent (50 percent for reserved categories), or a four-year bachelor's at 75 percent. JRF age limit is 30, with up to 5 years of relaxation for listed categories.
A plain three-year BSc does not qualify.

MSc or integrated MSc in Chemistry with 60 percent in the MSc and 60 percent in the BSc, Physics up to BSc level and Mathematics at Class 12 or BSc level. Age up to 26 for the general category on 1 August 2026.

items.heading: Pick Two Routes, Not Ten
items.text: Pick two routes, not ten. Run both through the four questions and set the rest aside.

items.heading: Read Ten Live Postings
items.text: Read ten live postings for each. Write down the instruments, tests and rule names that repeat, such as HPLC, GC, UV, titration, ISO/IEC 17025 or GMP.

items.heading: Make One Piece of Proof
items.text: Make one piece of proof for each. A calibration workbook, an SOP rewrite or a recorded lesson. Go at your own pace. Some people finish in a few weeks, others need a couple of months.

items.heading: Ask Three People Who Do
items.text: Ask three people who do the work. One from each route and one who left it. Ask what the first year felt like and what the safety training was like.
